verdict.summary: OpenWeather does not offer OAuth. You authenticate with an API key from your own account, sent as the appid parameter. There are no OAuth apps, scopes, test users or app review. The real limits are account-level call quotas, billing and data licensing terms.
verdict.time_to_first_connection: About 15 min of work, plus up to 2 hours for the key to activate
verdict.approval_wait: none (the key activates automatically within 2 hours)

gates.unlocks: Higher call volumes for a public product. OpenWeather has no app store, listing or app-review process. The Marketplace sells historical data, not app listings.

steps.title: Confirm the integration path is API key, not OAuth
steps.detail: OpenWeather publishes no OAuth or OIDC endpoints. /oauth/authorize and /.well-known/openid-configuration both return 404. Plan to send an API key as the appid parameter. You won't register an OAuth app or set a redirect URI.
gotchas: The Bot Forum 'agents' data lane is run by a different company and is not an OpenWeather OAuth path

steps.title: Create an OpenWeather account
steps.detail: Sign up at home.openweathermap.org. Use an account you control long-term, because limits and billing are tied to the account.

steps.title: Verify your email address
steps.detail: Click the verification link OpenWeather sends you. Your personal API key (APPID) is issued only after your email is verified.

steps.title: Copy or create a key on the API keys page
steps.detail: Sign in and open the account's 'API keys' page. Copy the default key, or create a named key for this integration. You can create as many keys as you like.
gotchas: All keys share one account-level quota, so extra keys don't add capacity

steps.title: Wait for key activation
steps.detail: New keys activate automatically up to 2 hours after registration. Calls made before then may fail.

steps.title: Run a test call with the key
steps.detail: Send a GET request to a Weather API endpoint (for example, current weather) and add the key as the appid query parameter. A successful JSON response means the key is active.

steps.title: Store the key as a credential in your integration
steps.detail: Composio has no OpenWeatherMap toolkit and no managed OAuth. Store the key in a custom tool or integration that accepts an API-key credential, and keep it server-side.
gotchas: OpenWeather support won't help with how the key is used inside third-party apps

steps.title: Set usage limits and monitor quota
steps.detail: If you use One Call API, review the daily call limit in your account (default 2,000; the first 1,000/day are free). Watch total account usage. On the free plan, if you exceed limits and don't respond to OpenWeather's notice, your key is suspended.
gotchas: If you're blocked after hitting the daily limit, raising the limit doesn't lift the block until the next 00:00-00:05 UTC reset unless you contact support

steps.title: Subscribe to a paid plan if you need more volume
steps.detail: In your account, open the 'Billing plans' tab and subscribe to a tier (Startup, Developer, Professional or Expert). Card payments are charged once the order is confirmed; bank transfer is invoiced manually.

steps.title: Review data licensing before shipping a product
steps.detail: Read OpenWeather's terms of sale. Data is licensed under ODbL and services under CC BY-SA 4.0, and you must keep copyright markings intact. Contact OpenWeather if you plan to redistribute data inside your product.

requirements.item: Verified email on an OpenWeather account
requirements.detail: You get an API key only after your email is verified.
Allow up to 2 hours after registration before the key works.
Usage from all keys and products is combined. On the free plan, overuse leads to suspension if you don't respond to OpenWeather's notice.
Subscribe from the 'Billing plans' tab in your account.

requirements.item: Compliance with licensing terms (ODbL / CC BY-SA 4.0, terms of sale)
requirements.detail: The licence is personal to the buyer and non-exclusive. Share-alike terms are relevant if you redistribute data.

scopes.effect: There are no scopes and no scope review. The key grants access to whatever products your account is subscribed to.

blockers.symptom: Looking for an OAuth client ID/secret or authorize URL: openweathermap.org/oauth/authorize returns 404
blockers.cause: OpenWeather has no OAuth app model. It uses API keys only.
blockers.fix: Use an API key from the account's API keys page and pass it as appid.

blockers.symptom: API calls fail right after you sign up
blockers.cause: New keys can take up to 2 hours to activate.
blockers.fix: Wait up to 2 hours, then retry.

blockers.cause: You exceeded the free-plan or daily limits and didn't respond to OpenWeather's notice.
blockers.fix: Upgrade your plan or reduce calls. Daily blocks clear at the 00:00-00:05 UTC reset, or contact support to lift one sooner.

blockers.symptom: OpenWeather support won't help with the integration
blockers.cause: Support doesn't cover how a key is used inside third-party applications.
blockers.fix: Debug the integration yourself. Contact support only about your account, keys, subscriptions or endpoint access.

composio.note: Composio has no OpenWeatherMap toolkit and no managed OAuth app, and OpenWeather itself offers no OAuth. There is nothing to switch from 'managed' to 'own app'. Get an API key from your OpenWeather account and supply it as a credential to a custom tool or integration that accepts API keys.

evidence.claim: OpenWeather's 'How to start' page says the API key alone is enough to call its weather APIs, and that its platform processes only requests that include a key.
evidence.quote: The API key is all you need to call any of our weather APIs.

evidence.claim: Free Weather API access lists 60 API calls per minute and 1,000,000 calls per month, for current weather, 3-hour forecast, air pollution, weather maps and geocoding.

The paid Weather API tiers (Startup, Developer, Professional, Expert) list per-minute and per-month call caps, and availability and update frequency vary by tier. Startup is listed at 40 USD per month with 600 calls per minute and 10M calls per month.
One Call API (pay-per-call) includes the first 1,000 calls per day free, and each further call is billed. The FAQ says the default daily limit is 2,000 calls, which the user can change.
evidence.quote: 1,000 API calls per day are included for free.

evidence.claim: Exceeding limits on the free plan leads to a notification asking the user to upgrade or reduce calls, and account suspension if no response is received. On paid plans the provider contacts the user to find a solution.
evidence.quote: In case we don't hear back from you, your API key will be suspended.

evidence.claim: Daily API call limits reset every day between 00:00 and 00:05 UTC. If an account is blocked after reaching a daily limit, raising the limit does not lift the block until the next reset, unless the user contacts support.
evidence.quote: Daily API call limits are reset every day between 00:00 and 00:05 UTC.

evidence.claim: The main site offers no third-party app store, app listing, or app-review process. The marketplace link leads to data archives and bulk data products, not an app directory.
The Marketplace page on the provider site sells historical data products. Its own FAQ points to it for one-time exports of historical data for a list of locations.
evidence.quote: You can request data via APIs or by a one-time export of historical data

evidence.claim: Support covers OpenWeather accounts, API keys, subscriptions and endpoint access. It does not cover how an API key is used inside third-party applications, which the developer of that application handles.
No OAuth scopes exist. Access is controlled by an API key sent as an appid query parameter or equivalent, so no scope review or sensitive-scope classification applies.
evidence.quote: add your API key as an *appid* parameter to the GET request

evidence.claim: Terms of sale grant a licence to use purchased digital content (not ownership), which is personal to the buyer and non-exclusive. The buyer must keep copyright and ownership markings intact.
evidence.quote: When you buy any digital content and download it, you will not own it. Instead we give you permission to use it

evidence.claim: OpenWeather says it does not support using its API key inside third-party applications and that such apps are owned and configured by their developers.
evidence.quote: we do not provide technical support for using an OpenWeather API key inside third-party applications

evidence.claim: The terms say products and services are provided under CC BY-SA 4.0, and data and databases are licensed under ODbL. Share-alike terms are therefore relevant to redistributing data inside a product.
evidence.quote: Data and database are open and licensed by Open Data Commons Open Database License (ODbL).

evidence.claim: Paid subscriptions are bought by signing up, opening the Billing plans tab in the account, and subscribing. The terms say card payments are charged once the order is confirmed; bank transfer is by manual invoicing.
evidence.quote: Sign up on the website, choose Billing plans tab at your account and subscribe

evidence.claim: A separate 'agents' product (The Bot Forum) issues data keys through its own signup. OpenWeather states this is a different operator and is not an OpenWeather product. It is not an OAuth app path for this provider.
evidence.quote: The lane is operated and sold by Extreme Electronics Ltd, trading as The Bot Forum

evidence.claim: Developer docs are on openweathermap.org/api, and the site's main call to action is 'Get API Key'. The API reference covers the current, forecast, One Call and other products.

The conventional OAuth authorize path on openweathermap.org returned HTTP 404 when probed with an invalid client and the Composio callback. The page title was 'OpenWeather | Business' and no OAuth error parameters came back, so no live developer-OAuth authorize endpoint was evident.
OpenID Connect discovery at openweathermap.org returned 404, so no OIDC configuration is published.
API keys are created from the account's 'API keys' page, which is behind a sign-in wall. Probing that URL redirected to the sign-in page.
Getting a key means signing up, verifying email, and then copying the key from the account page. The provider's FAQ describes this flow.
evidence.quote: Once your account is created and your email address is verified, you will receive your personal API key (APPID)

evidence.claim: A new API key is activated automatically, up to 2 hours after registration.
evidence.quote: Your API key will be activated automatically, up to 2 hours after your successful registration.

evidence.claim: The provider states it does not limit keys per developer. Developers can create as many keys as they like, and usage across all keys on an account counts toward the same account limits.
evidence.quote: You can create as many keys as you like.

evidence.claim: API call limits apply at the account level, not per API key or per product, and usage from all keys and subscribed products is combined.
evidence.quote: API call limits are applied at the account level, not per API key or per product.

open_questions: Whether OpenWeather allows redistributing its data inside a third-party product under ODbL/CC BY-SA and its terms of sale was not confirmed. Contact OpenWeather before shipping.
Exact paid-tier prices and caps could not be fully verified. Re-check openweathermap.org/price before quoting numbers. Third-party sources report inconsistent figures across pages.
No OpenWeather position on Composio-brokered or agent integrations was found.
OpenWeather publishes no developer changelog, so recent changes to key or usage policies could not be checked.
